note: Attack chains, stage by stage, with the checks that show the condition each stage needs on a host. Hand-written from public reporting and from what a snapshot can actually show; no catalog is downloaded and nothing here is executed. A stage drawn as open means the condition for it is in the configuration of that host, not that anything ran; a complete chain means every stage of it has at least one enabling condition on the same host, which is evidence worth acting on, not a demonstrated exploit. Every check named here must exist in the catalog and every stage must exist in stages (the regression checks both).

paths.name: Paste-and-run lure to credential theft
paths.why: The ClickFix and FileFix lures of 2024-26 need no exploit: the user pastes the command, the script layer runs it, the antivirus is out of the way, and the credentials are read out of LSASS.

steps.needs: the user can be talked into running a pasted command, and Windows does not stop a downloaded script
an interpreter that runs unconstrained and can reach the internet
the antivirus can be blinded or does not cover the drop folder
credentials readable in memory or kept in the local cache
a reusable secret or an unauthenticated path to the next host

paths.name: Macro document to persistence
paths.why: The oldest chain still in use: an Office document that is allowed to run code, an interpreter that fetches the next stage, and a load point that survives the reboot.

steps.needs: a document can run code without a prompt, or from a folder that is trusted
a signed Windows binary can fetch and run the next stage
a load point the payload can write and that starts it again

paths.name: Standard user to SYSTEM
paths.why: Code running as the logged-on user becomes SYSTEM by writing a file or a registry value that a privileged process reads, and the elevation prompt does not get in the way.

steps.needs: a place a non-administrator can write that a privileged process loads or starts
elevation happens without a prompt, or the administrator token is handed over unfiltered
once elevated, the credentials in memory are readable
a privileged load point to come back through

paths.name: Vulnerable driver to the kernel and the security agent
paths.why: Bring your own vulnerable driver: a signed driver with a known flaw gives kernel access, and from there the agent that would have reported the rest is stopped.

steps.needs: a vulnerable signed driver can be loaded, or the blocklist and the integrity settings are off
the security agent is missing or can be turned off, and the event log keeps no trace of it
credentials not held in an isolated process

paths.name: Name resolution relay to lateral movement
paths.why: A broadcast name lookup nobody needs is answered by the attacker, the authentication that follows is relayed, and the next service accepts it because nothing is signed.

steps.needs: a broadcast or legacy name lookup an attacker on the segment can answer
the authentication that follows is weak enough to be used again
a service that accepts a relayed session because nothing is signed

paths.name: Exposed remote service to session takeover
paths.why: The way in is a service that answers from the network; the way on is the credentials that service is allowed to hand to the next hop, or a session already open on the host.

steps.needs: a service answering from the network, or a firewall that does not stop it
credentials delegated to whatever host asks, or an authentication the host does not pin
a session to take over, a pivot to set up, or one password that opens every host

paths.name: Stolen laptop to the data on the disk
paths.why: No network is involved: the disk is read in another machine, or the recovery environment and an unattended unlock give the session away.

steps.needs: the volume can be read without the user, the session is left unlocked, or the boot chain can be changed
secrets kept on that disk: cached logons, a stored password, an automatic logon

paths.name: Browser extension to the session cookies
paths.why: The infostealer campaigns of 2024-26 do not need the password: an extension with broad access, or an unprotected cookie store, hands over a session that is already authenticated.

steps.needs: an extension that can read every page, sideloaded or pulled from the store after the fact
a session store or a credential store that can be read from the user's own session

paths.name: Ransomware with the brakes off
paths.why: What turns an infection into an outage is not the encryption but what is missing around it: no behaviour blocking, no shadow copies to restore from, writable shares to spread into.

steps.needs: behaviour blocking and folder protection are not in the way
nothing to restore from, and a share to spread the damage through

paths.name: Domain controller taken from the network
paths.why: The chain that ends a domain: a service on the controller that answers anyone, authentication that can be downgraded or replayed, and a privileged logon nothing restricts.

steps.needs: a service on the controller that answers from the network, or a channel it does not protect
authentication that can be downgraded, accounts that can be listed without credentials, or a recovery account that answers from the network
a privileged logon nothing restricts, or a session path onto the controller itself

paths.name: Known-vulnerable software to code on the host
paths.why: The way in that needs no lure: a browser, a reader, a VPN client or a server component with a published flaw, none of the mitigations that would stop the exploit from becoming code, and an antivirus that can be set aside before the payload lands.

steps.needs: software with a known flaw, or a version that no longer gets fixes
none of the mitigations that would stop the exploit from turning into code
an antivirus that can be set aside, does not look where the payload lands, or is told to let it run

paths.name: Anonymous access to a local administrator account
paths.why: Nothing is exploited: the host answers a request that carries no credentials, says which accounts it has, accepts a password that is weak, missing or replayed, and the account that opens it opens the next host too.

steps.needs: the host answers a request that carries no credentials
the accounts can be listed, and a password guessed, left blank or replayed
the account that opens this host is privileged, and not unique to it

paths.name: Print spooler to SYSTEM
paths.why: PrintNightmare and the point-and-print bypasses after it: a spooler running where nothing prints, a driver a non-administrator is allowed to install, and the print load point it leaves behind starts as SYSTEM at every boot.

steps.needs: a spooler that runs where it is not needed, and a driver a non-administrator may install
a load point the spooler itself reads at every boot
nothing that stops an unexpected driver from loading, or records that it did

paths.name: Secrets left on the disk to a privileged account
paths.why: The credentials are not taken out of memory, they are found: an answer file from the deployment, a cached group policy preference, a password in the vault or a key in a profile, belonging to an account that is an administrator here and on the next host.

steps.needs: a secret written on the disk and readable from a session on this host
the account that secret belongs to is privileged on this host
the same secret is accepted by the next host

paths.name: Removable media to execution
paths.why: The USB drop and the walk-up: the media runs on insert or the file runs on a double click, the interpreter is unconstrained, and a load point keeps it after the stick is gone.

steps.needs: media that runs on insert, or a file that runs on a double click with nothing to warn about where it came from
an interpreter that runs unconstrained, and no list of what may run
a load point the payload can write and that starts it again
